description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, generously studded with an assortment of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. Its crispy edges and tender interior make it a perfect appetizer or a light meal, especially on a rainy day. Served with a tangy dipping sauce, this dish offers a delightful blend of textures and umami flavors.

ingredients.notes: or anchovy broth for more flavor

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and red pepper flakes. Stir well and set aside. This sauce will complement the rich flavor of your Haemul Pajeon.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, cornstarch, salt, egg, and cold water until smooth. Be careful not to overmix; a few small lumps are acceptable. The batter should have a consistency similar to thin pancake batter.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Ensure your assorted seafood is thoroughly cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces. Add the seafood and thinly sliced onion to the batter, mixing gently to coat everything evenly. This ensures even distribution in your pancake.

instructions.title: Cook the First Side of the Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil. Pour about half of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake. Immediately arrange about half of the green onion pieces on top of the batter, pressing them gently into the mixture.

instructions.title: Flip and Cook the Second Side
instructions.text: Cook for 3-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Drizzle another tablespoon of oil around the edges, then carefully flip the pancake. Continue cooking for another 3-5 minutes until the other side is golden brown and the seafood is cooked through. The green onions should be slightly charred.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board and cut into wedges. Repeat with the remaining batter, green onions, and oil to make a second pancake. Garnish with thinly sliced red chili if desired. Serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce.

tips: For extra crispiness, use a combination of all-purpose flour and rice flour in your batter, or add a splash of sparkling water.
Feel free to customize the seafood mix with clams, oysters, or even imitation crab meat. Ensure all seafood is fresh and properly cleaned.
Serve Haemul Pajeon hot off the pan for the best texture. It pairs wonderfully with a cold makgeolli (Korean rice wine) or a light beer.
article:
Korean cuisine is a treasure trove of flavors, textures, and culinary delights, and among its most beloved dishes is the Haemul Pajeon. This savory seafood and scallion pancake is a staple in Korean households, street food stalls, and restaurants alike, celebrated for its crispy edges, tender interior, and a delightful medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. Whether you’re a seasoned fan of Korean food or just beginning your culinary exploration, Haemul Pajeon offers a delightful introduction to the country's rich gastronomic heritage. It’s more than just a pancake; it’s a comforting, satisfying, and endlessly customizable dish that embodies the spirit of Korean home cooking.

## What is Haemul Pajeon? (Korean Seafood Pancake)

At its heart, Haemul Pajeon is a type of jeon, which refers to any dish made by pan-frying ingredients coated in an egg and flour batter. The name "Haemul Pajeon" itself tells you exactly what it is: "Haemul" means seafood, and "Pa" refers to scallions or green onions, while "jeon" is the pancake. What sets it apart is the generous amount of fresh scallions that form the backbone of the pancake, often laid out in long strands, creating a visually appealing and texturally interesting base. Interspersed within this green canvas are various types of seafood, which become succulent and flavorful as they cook within the delicate, crisp batter. The result is a savory pancake that is simultaneously crispy on the outside and wonderfully soft and flavorful on the inside, often served with a tangy, savory dipping sauce that perfectly complements its richness. It’s a dish that appeals to all senses, making it a popular appetizer, snack, or even a light meal.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon starts with fresh, quality ingredients. Here’s what you’ll typically need:

For the Batter:
*   **All-purpose flour:** The base of your pancake.
*   **Rice flour or cornstarch (optional but recommended):** Adding a small amount of rice flour or cornstarch to your batter contributes significantly to a crispier texture.
*   **Cold water or anchovy broth:** Using cold liquid helps prevent gluten development, resulting in a more tender and crispy pancake. Anchovy broth adds a layer of umami.
*   **Egg:** Binds the batter and adds richness.
*   **Salt:** For seasoning the batter.

For the Seafood and Vegetables:
*   **Scallions (green onions):** The star of the show! You'll need a generous bunch, ideally the thicker, white parts, cut into 3-4 inch lengths.
*   **Assorted seafood (Haemul):** A mix works best. Common choices include small shrimp (peeled and deveined), squid (sliced into rings), mussels, oysters, or even clams. Fresh is always preferred, but high-quality frozen seafood works well too.
*   **Optional vegetables:** Thinly sliced onion, red or green chili peppers (for a touch of heat and color), or carrots can be added for extra flavor and visual appeal.

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   **Soy sauce:** The base of the sauce.
*   **Rice vinegar:** Adds tanginess.
*   **Sesame oil:** For a nutty aroma.
*   **Toasted sesame seeds:** For texture and flavor.
*   **Gochugaru (Korean chili flakes):** Optional, for a slight kick.
*   **Minced garlic:** For aromatic depth.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Haemul Pajeon

Making Haemul Pajeon at home is surprisingly straightforward, yielding incredibly rewarding results.

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** Thoroughly wash your chosen seafood. If using squid, slice it into bite-sized rings. Peel and devein shrimp. Cut the scallions into 3-4 inch pieces. If using other vegetables, slice them thinly. Set aside.
2.  **Make the Dipping Sauce:** In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, gochugaru (if using), and minced garlic. Stir well and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour (or cornstarch), and salt. Gradually add the cold water or broth while whisking until a smooth, thin batter forms. It should be slightly thinner than pancake batter. Beat in the egg. Be careful not to overmix; a few lumps are perfectly fine.
4.  **Combine Ingredients:** Gently fold most of the prepared seafood and about half of the scallion pieces into the batter. You want the seafood and scallions to be coated, but not swimming in too much batter.
5.  **Cook the Pancake:** Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of cooking oil (about 2-3 tablespoons). Once the oil is hot, pour about a cup of the batter mixture into the pan, spreading it out evenly to form a round pancake. Immediately arrange the remaining scallion pieces and a few extra pieces of seafood on top of the raw batter.
6.  **Flip and Finish:** Cook for 4-5 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy and the edges begin to set. Drizzle a little more oil around the edges. Carefully flip the pancake. You can use a large spatula or slide it onto a plate and invert it back into the pan. Cook for another 3-4 minutes on the second side until golden brown and cooked through.
7.  **Serve:** Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges, like a pizza, and serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat the process for any remaining batter.

## Tips for the Perfect Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that ideal crispy-on-the-outside, tender-on-the-inside texture for your Haemul Pajeon requires a few key techniques:

*   **Keep it Cold:** Using very cold water or even ice water for your batter is crucial. It helps to inhibit gluten formation, leading to a lighter, crispier pancake.
*   **Don't Overmix:** A slightly lumpy batter is better than an overmixed one. Overmixing develops gluten, making the pancake tough.
*   **Generous Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil! A good amount of oil in the hot pan is essential for those coveted crispy edges and a beautifully golden crust.
*   **Hot Pan, Then Medium:** Start with a hot pan to get an initial sear and crispness, then reduce the heat slightly to medium to ensure the pancake cooks through without burning.
*   **Plenty of Scallions:** The "Pa" in Pajeon is not just an accent; it's a main ingredient. Don't skimp on the scallions; they provide much of the flavor and structure.
*   **Don't Overcrowd:** Cook one pancake at a time, or two if your pan is very large. Overcrowding lowers the pan temperature and prevents proper crisping.
*   **Rice Flour for Crispiness:** If you want that extra-crispy exterior, the addition of rice flour is non-negotiable. It gives a distinct crunch that all-purpose flour alone can't achieve.

## Serving Your Haemul Pajeon

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed fresh off the pan, while it's still warm and crispy. Slice it into wedges, making it easy to share and dip. The accompanying dipping sauce is an absolute must, as its tangy, savory notes cut through the richness of the pancake beautifully.

In Korea, Haemul Pajeon is often paired with traditional alcoholic beverages. Makgeolli, a milky, lightly carbonated Korean rice wine, is a classic accompaniment, its subtle sweetness and effervescence providing a wonderful contrast. Soju, a clear distilled spirit, or a cold beer are also popular choices. As an appetizer, it's perfect for sharing with friends and family. It can also serve as a satisfying light meal, especially when accompanied by a side of kimchi or other banchan (small side dishes).

## Haemul Pajeon Variations & Substitutions

The beauty of jeon lies in its versatility, and Haemul Pajeon is no exception. While the classic seafood and scallion combination is heavenly, you can easily adapt the recipe to suit your preferences or what you have on hand.

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** For a meat-free option, simply omit the seafood. You can load it up with various vegetables like thinly sliced mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, or king oyster work well), zucchini, bell peppers, or even kimchi for a kimchi pajeon (kimchi-jeon).
*   **Kimchi Pajeon (Kimchi-jeon):** A hugely popular variation, this involves adding chopped, well-fermented kimchi to the batter. The sourness and spice of the kimchi create an incredibly flavorful pancake.
*   **Meat Pajeon (Gogi Pajeon):** While Haemul Pajeon focuses on seafood, you can also make a meat version using thinly sliced beef (bulgogi style) or pork.
*   **Seasonal Vegetables:** Feel free to experiment with seasonal vegetables. Asparagus, sweet potato, or even finely shredded cabbage can make interesting additions.
*   **Gluten-Free Option:** For those with gluten sensitivities, you can substitute the all-purpose flour with a good quality gluten-free flour blend, ensuring your rice flour ratio is maintained for crispiness.

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a dish; it's an experience. It’s a testament to the simple yet profound flavors of Korean cuisine, offering comfort, crunch, and a burst of savory goodness in every bite. Whether you stick to the traditional recipe or venture into creative variations, making this Korean seafood pancake at home is a rewarding culinary adventure that will undoubtedly impress your taste buds and those of your loved ones. So, gather your ingredients, heat up your pan, and get ready to enjoy a truly authentic taste of Korea.
